MAJAZ:v1p14/r12.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r12.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r12.claim: Qawm (‘people’) is used with both feminine and masculine agreement, as shown by the two cited forms.
MAJAZ:v1p14/r12.anchor: وقال: «كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين» (26/ 105) يقال: هذه قومك، وجاء قومك.

STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r7.claim: Noah's story stresses his people's aversion to followers of low social status.
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r7.anchor: Next told is Noah’s story (vv. 105–21), with emphasis on his people’s aversion to the individuals of low social status who followed him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r9.claim: Although qawm is grammatically feminine as a collective, masculine pronouns refer to its male rational members.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r9.anchor: القوم: مؤنث مجازي التأنيث، ويصغر قويمة، فلذلك جاء: كذبت قوم نوح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r10.claim: An alternative treats qawm as masculine and explains the feminine verb by its sense of community or nation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r10.anchor: وقيل: قوم مذكر، وأنث لأنه في معنى الأمة والجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r11.claim: The earlier discussion of Noah's people being said to deny the messengers despite one messenger is linked to the wording in al-Furqān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p174/r11.anchor: وتقدم معنى تكذيب قوم نوح المرسلين، وإن كان المرسل إليهم واحدا في الفرقان

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p426/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p426/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p426/r4.claim: The next section recounts Noah's message to his people, their rejection, and the ensuing punishment, and closes with the repeated refrain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p426/r4.anchor: the anecdote of Noah is covered. His message to his nation, their rejection

RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r1.claim: After recounting Moses and Abraham, God recounts Noah to console Muhammad for what he faces from his people; Noah preached for 950 years and was still denied.
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r1.anchor: قص على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم خبر موسى وإبراهيم تسلية له

RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r2.claim: The singular feminine verb كذبت agrees with قوم because the collective noun is grammatically feminine; its diminutive is قويمة.

RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r3.claim: One explanation is that although Noah’s people denied Noah, this entails denying the other messengers because the way their prophethood is known does not differ.
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r3.anchor: أنهم وإن كذبوا نوحا لكن تكذيبه في المعنى يتضمن تكذيب غيره

RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r4.claim: Alternatively, Noah’s people denied all God’s messengers, perhaps because they were unbelieving materialists or Brahmins.
RAZI-FULL:v24p133/r4.anchor: أن قوم نوح كذبوا بجميع رسل الله تعالى ، إما لأنهم كانوا من الزنادقة

RAZI-FULL:v24p133#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p133#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p133#2/r15.claim: Rāzī says Noah’s story has already been explained at length in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf and Sūrat Hūd.
RAZI-FULL:v24p133#2/r15.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في قصته مشروحا في سورة الأعراف وسورة هود

BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r1.claim: The perfect verb conveys continuing denial from the beginning of Noah’s preaching through its end.
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r1.anchor: تكذيبا مستمرا من حين الدعوة إلى انتهائها.

BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r2.claim: Qawm can mean a group including men and women, or men specifically with women included by subordination; its feminine diminutive is qūwayma.
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r2.anchor: القوم الجماعة من الرجال والنساء معا أو الرجال خاصة وتدخل النساء على التبعية ويؤنث بدليل مجيء تصغيره على قويمة

BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r3.claim: “The messengers” means Noah alone, while the plural reflects that denying one messenger denies all who share tawḥīd and basic law, or because each messenger commands belief in all.
BURSEVI:v6p211#3/r3.anchor: أي : نوحا وحده والجمع باعتبار أن من كذب رسولا واحدا فقد كذب الجميع لاجتماع الكل على التوحيد وأصول الشرائع

STUDYQURAN:26:105/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r1.claim: The Noah narrative is also related in several other Quranic passages, including Sūrah 71.
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r1.anchor: For the story of Noah, also see 7:59–64; 10:71–73; 11:25–48;

STUDYQURAN:26:105/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r2.claim: Although Noah is singular, his people's denial of him implies rejection of all messengers because the path to recognizing a messenger is universal across history, and each messenger calls people to affirm all messengers.
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r2.anchor: the people’s denial of him would include the rejection of all messengers, since the path to recognizing and affirming a messenger is universal

STUDYQURAN:26:105/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that they rejected Noah's prophecy that messengers would come after him.
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r3.anchor: a category stands for a specific individual (Q)

STUDYQURAN:26:105/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r4.claim: A further explanation is that the plural category of messengers stands for Noah as a specific individual.
STUDYQURAN:26:105/r4.anchor: or it may be an example in which a category stands for a specific individual (Q).

TAB-FULL:v17p601#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p601#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p601#2/r1.claim: Noah’s people denied God’s messengers when their brother Noah called them to fear the punishment for disbelief and denying the messengers.
TAB-FULL:v17p601#2/r1.anchor: الله {أمين} [الأعراف: 68] على وحيه إلي، برسالته إياي إليكم.

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r1.claim: After the stories of Moses and Abraham, the account turns to Noah, the first of the foremost prophets; most of his people disbelieved, so God drowned them and saved Noah and the believers with him.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r1.anchor: وهو أول أولي العزم سادة الأنبياء

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r2.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r2.claim: Al-Mufradat says qawm originally denotes a group of men, not women, citing the verse about one people not mocking another and a poet's contrast between men and women.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r2.anchor: قال في المفردات القوم جماعة الرجال في الأصل دون النساء

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r3.speaker: الشاعر
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r3.claim: The cited line “Are the people of Al-Hisn men or women?” uses qawm to mean a group of men.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر أقوم آل حصن أم نساء

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r4.claim: One grammatical analysis treats qawm as masculine and explains a feminine predicate by taking the word to mean a collective group.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r4.anchor: ولفظ القوم قيل مذكر وتأنيث الفعل المسند إليه بتأويل الجماعة

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r5.claim: A second analysis treats qawm itself as feminine.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r5.anchor: وقيل مؤنث وقال في المصباح يذكر ويؤنث

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r6.claim: Although qawm originally names men, in most Qur'anic usage it denotes both men and women.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r6.anchor: وفي عامة القرآن أريدوا به والنساء جميعا

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r7.claim: Noah's people are called deniers of all messengers because their call to monotheism was one unified message, so rejecting Noah amounted to rejecting them all; God likewise counts belief in some messengers but not others as disbelief in all.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r7.anchor: إنما هو من جهة أن دعوتهم واحدة وكلمتهم متفقة على التوحيد

TABATABAI:26:105-110/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r8.claim: Another explanation takes the plural generically, like saying someone rides mounts and wears cloaks though he has only one of each; al-Tabatabai prefers the unified-message explanation, and the same alternatives apply to the accounts of ʿAd and Thamud.
TABATABAI:26:105-110/r8.anchor: وقيل هو من قبيل قولهم فلان يركب الدواب ويلبس البرود

TABRISI:26:105-111/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:105-111/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:105-111/r12.claim: The feminine verb agrees with قوم in its intended sense of a group, although the noun is grammatically masculine.
TABRISI:26:105-111/r12.anchor: دخلت التاء في كذبت والقوم مذكر لأن المراد بالقوم الجماعة أي كذبت جماعة نوح المرسلين

TABRISI:26:105-111/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:105-111/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:105-111/r13.claim: Denying one of God's messengers counts as denying them all, since every messenger commands belief in all messengers.
TABRISI:26:105-111/r13.anchor: لأن من كذب رسولا واحدا من رسل الله فقد كذب الجماعة لأن كل رسول يأمر بتصديق جميع الرسل.

TABRISI:26:105-111/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:105-111/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:26:105-111/r14.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says the messengers are Noah and the prophets between him and Adam.
TABRISI:26:105-111/r14.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر ع: يعني بالمرسلين نوحا والأنبياء الذين كانوا بينه وبين آدم

THALABI:v7p172#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p172#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p172#2/r1.claim: The feminine singular verb agrees with the collective people, as in the Quranic expression “the Bedouins said.”
THALABI:v7p172#2/r1.anchor: كذبت قوم نوح ادخلت التاء للجماعة كقوله قالت الأعراب

THALABI:v7p172#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p172#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p172#2/r2.claim: “The messengers” refers to Noah alone, as in the address “O messengers.”
THALABI:v7p172#2/r2.anchor: المرسلين يعني نوحا وحده كقوله يا أيها الرسل

THALABI:v7p172#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p172#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p172#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says each later messenger brought what the earlier one brought, so denying one messenger is denying all of them.
THALABI:v7p172#2/r3.anchor: عن الحسين قال: قيل له: يا أبا سعيد أرأيت قوله عز وجل كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r1.claim: The feminine verb is used with masculine qawm because the intended sense is the group, jamāʿat qawm Nūḥ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r2.claim: The plural messengers refers specifically to Noah; rejecting one messenger is rejecting them all, since each commands belief in all messengers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومقاتل، والمفسرون: يعني نوحا وحده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the last messenger brings what the first brought, so rejecting one is rejecting them all.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الحسن؛ لما سئل عن هذا وأمثاله فقال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī means Noah and what he told them about later messengers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي {كذبت قوم نوح} نوحا، وما أخبرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows that they rejected all messengers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p82/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: وجائز أن يكونوا كذبوا جميع الرسل

ELMALILI:26:105-122/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:105-122/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:105-122/r1.claim: Noah's people rejected the messengers sent to them.
ELMALILI:26:105-122/r1.anchor: Nûh kavmi gönderilen resulleri tekzib etti (105).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:105/r1.claim: Noah’s call has the same essential principles as Moses’s and Abraham’s, and their peoples’ beliefs and responses to true religion were alike; the three narrative groups deliver the same message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:105/r1.anchor: Sonuç itibariyle her üç peygambere dair âyetler grubunda da aynı mesajlar verilmiştir

BURHAN:v2p238/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p238/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p238/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says 'the messengers' means Noah alone, like saying someone rides mounts and wears cloaks though he has only one of each.
BURHAN:v2p238/r2.anchor: والمراد بالمرسلين نوح كقولك فلان يركب الدواب ويلبس البرود

BURHAN:v3p150/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p150/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p150/r3.claim: The feminine verb in 'Noah's people denied' reflects an understood feminine construct; without that understood noun, qawm would take a masculine verb.
BURHAN:v3p150/r3.anchor: ولولا ذلك لحذفت التاء لأن القوم مذكر

SAMIN-DURR:26:105/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:105/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:105/r1.claim: The verb is feminine because qawm is grammatically feminine, as its diminutive quwayma shows, or because qawm means umma; the later pronoun is masculine by predominance of male members.
SAMIN-DURR:26:105/r1.anchor: إنما أنث فعل القوم؛ لأنه مؤنث بدليل تصغيره على قويمة

ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r1.claim: The feminine verb agrees with the collective sense جماعة قوم نوح, even though قوم is grammatically masculine.
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r1.anchor: دخلت التاء وقوم نوح مذكرون، لأن المعنى كذبت جماعة قوم نوح

ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r2.claim: One possible reading is that Noah alone was denied; whoever rejects one of God's messengers rejects the whole company, since each messenger calls people to affirm all messengers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونوا كذبوا نوحا وحده، ومن كذب رسولا واحدا من رسل الله فقد كذب الجماعة

ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r3.claim: Another possible explanation is that Noah's people denied all the messengers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p95/r3.anchor: وجائز أن يكون كذبت جميع الرسل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r1.claim: Noah's people denied only Noah, yet the plural messengers is used because all messengers conveyed the same message; rejecting Noah thus rejects every messenger, and rejecters share a mentality and fate. Abraham's story warns Muhammad's opponents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r1.anchor: The people of Noah (sws) had only denied one messenger: Noah (sws). However, the plural “messengers” is used

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r2.claim: Acceptance and rejection reflect a people's mentality; rejecting Noah's message amounts to rejecting every messenger, whose rejecters share a mentality and fate. Abraham's story warns those rejecting Muhammad.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p427/r2.anchor: the real basis of acceptance or rejection is the mentality of people

ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r1.claim: قوم can be masculine or feminine, like other collective nouns without a singular from the same form; its feminine verb may treat the group as an الأمة or جماعت.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r1.anchor: القوم كما في المصباح يذكر ويؤنث وكذلك كل أسم جمع ولا واحد له من لفظه نحو رهط ونفر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r2.claim: Their collective denial counts as denial of all messengers because they agreed in monotheism and the fundamental laws that do not vary by age.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r2.anchor: تكذيبهم المرسلين باعتبار إجماع الكل على التوحيد وأصول الشرائع التي لاتختلف باختلاف الأزمنة والاعصار

ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, المرسلين means Noah alone, with the definite article used generically, as in saying someone rides mounts though he owns one mount.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p106#3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالمرسلين نوح عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p120/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p120/r13.speaker: الحسن البصري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p120/r13.claim: The author reports a question put to al-Hasan: why say Noah's people denied the messengers, and similarly speak of Ad and Thamud, when each had one messenger? The excerpt leaves the question unfinished.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p120/r13.anchor: قيل للحسن البصري: يا أبا سعيد أرأيت قوله: {كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين}

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:104-110/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:104-110/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:104-110/r2.claim: Qawm is grammatically feminine, as shown by its diminutive قويمة; their denial of Noah was discussed as denial of the messengers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:104-110/r2.anchor: ال { قوم } مؤنثة ولذلك تصغر على قويمة وقد مر الكلام في تكذيبهم المرسلين.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r8.claim: After Abraham, Noah’s account comes as that of the second father, older in time, showing that trial is ancient and displaying both long respite and eventual universal punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r8.anchor: قصة الأب الثاني , مقدما لها على غيرها , لما له من القدم في الزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r9.claim: The feminine verb form is deliberately chosen although masculine agreement with qawm is more common: it marks their deed as vile or their people as insignificant despite their power.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r9.anchor: اختيارا للتأنيث - وأن كان تذكير القوم أشهر -

BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r10.claim: Noah’s people means all humanity on earth before peoples divided through the separation of languages.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r10.anchor: وهو أهل الأرض كلهم من الآدميين قبل اختلاف الأمم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r11.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r11.claim: Al-Baghawī transmits the explanation that denying Noah amounts to denying all messengers, since one who rejects a single messenger’s miracle rejects what all brought.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p372/r11.anchor: من كذب بمعجزة واحدة فقد كذب الكل

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r1.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said Noah was the first prophet sent; no grading is stated.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r1.anchor: انس ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : اول نبي ارسل نوح

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r2.speaker: يزيد الرقاشي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r2.claim: Yazid al-Raqashi says Noah was named for his long lament over himself.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r2.anchor: يزيد الرقاشي ، قال : انما سمي نوحا لطول ما ناح

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Noah was sent at forty, preached among his people for 950 years, and lived sixty years after the Flood as people multiplied.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2787#2/r3.anchor: ابن عباس قال : بعث نوح وهو لاربعين سنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p157/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p157/r1.claim: The repeated formula of denying the messengers will introduce parallel accounts of the people of Ad, Thamud, Lot, and the Thicket.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p157/r1.anchor: وسيأتي حكاية تكذيب عاد وثمود وقوم لوط وأصحاب ليكة على هذا النمط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p159/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p159/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p159/r4.claim: The commentary refers readers to the earlier mention of Noah among those God chose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p159/r4.anchor: وتقدم ذكر نوح عند قوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r1.claim: The feminine verb agrees with قوم because the noun conveys the sense of a community or group.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r1.anchor: أسند كذبت إلى «القوم» وفيه علامة التأنيث من حيث القوم في معنى الأمة والجماعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r2.claim: Denying one prophet amounts to denying all messengers because their statement and call are one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p236#2/r2.anchor: من كذب نبيا واحدا، كذب جميع الأنبياء إذ قولهم واحد ودعوتهم سواء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p133#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p133#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p133#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the feminine verb with the masculine noun qawm by taking qawm to mean a group (jamāʿa).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p133#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج القوم مذكرون والمعنى كذبت جماعة قوم نوح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r1.claim: Noah was the first messenger sent to earth after people began worshiping idols; God sent him to forbid idolatry and warn of its punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r1.anchor: عن عبده ورسوله نوح، عليه السلام، وهو أول رسول بعث إلى الأرض بعدما عبدت الأصنام والأنداد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r2.claim: Although Noah alone was sent to them, denying him counts as denying all messengers because their shared message is one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p150#3/r2.anchor: تكذيبهم له بمنزلة تكذيب جميع الرسل

JISHUMI:v7p5370/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5370/r3.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p5370/r3.claim: Yaqub reads أتباعك الأرذلون with a separated initial alif, still tāʾ, and nominative ʿayn; this matches Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Ibn Abbas.
JISHUMI:v7p5370/r3.anchor: قرأ يعقوب: وأتباعك الأرذلون بقطع الألف وسكون التاء

JISHUMI:v7p5370/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5370/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
JISHUMI:v7p5370/r4.claim: Other readers have واتبعك as a connected form with doubled, open tāʾ and a past verb without alif; this matches Ibn Masud and is Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim's choice.
JISHUMI:v7p5370/r4.anchor: والباقون: واتبعك موصولة الألف مشددة التاء مفتوحة العين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r1.claim: The plural “messengers” refers to Noah alone, as when a plural category is used although someone owns only one item of it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r1.anchor: ونظير قوله : { المرسلين } والمراد نوح عليه السلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r2.claim: قوم is grammatically feminine, and its diminutive is قويمة.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p328#2/r2.anchor: القوم : مؤنثة ، وتصغيرها قويمة . ونظير قوله :

MUQATIL:26:105-111/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:105-111/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:105-111/r1.claim: Noah’s people denied Noah alone; the same pattern appears in the account in Surat al-Qamar (54:9).
MUQATIL:26:105-111/r1.anchor: يعنى كذبوا نوحا وحده، نظيرها فى اقتربت الساعة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r1.claim: The noun qawm can be masculine or feminine in agreement.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r2.claim: One report says Noah was born in Adam's lifetime.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r2.anchor: قيل ولد نوح فى زمن آدم عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r3.claim: “The messengers” is plural although only Noah is intended, as in saying someone rides mounts or wears cloaks while owning one of each.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r3.anchor: والمراد نوح عليه السلام قولك فلان يركب الدواب ويلبس البرود وماله إلا دابة أو برد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r4.claim: Alternatively, the people rejected messengership altogether, so the plural is apt.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r4.anchor: أو كانوا ينكرون بعث الرسل أصلا فلذا جمع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r5.claim: Rejecting one messenger is rejecting all, since each messenger calls people to believe in every messenger; Nasafi says the same applies throughout this sūra.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p191#4/r5.anchor: لأن من كذب واحدا منهم فقد كذب الكل لأن كل رسول يدعو الناس إلى الإيمان بجميع الرسل

QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r1.claim: The feminine verb treats the people as the group or congregation of Noah’s people.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r1.anchor: قال «كذبت» والقوم مذكر لأن المعنى كذبت جماعة قوم نوح

QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r2.claim: The plural “messengers” is used because denying one messenger entails denying all: every messenger commands belief in all messengers.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r2.anchor: وقال: { المرسلين } لأن من كذب رسولا فقد كذب الرسل لأن كل رسول يأمر بتصديق جميع الرسل

QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r3.claim: One view is that Noah’s people denied Noah’s prophethood and his report that messengers would come after him.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r3.anchor: وقيل: كذبوا نوحا في النبوة وفيما أخبرهم به من مجيء المرسلين بعده

QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r4.claim: Another view takes “the messengers” as a generic class while intending Noah in particular.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:105-106/r4.anchor: وقيل: ذكر الجنس والمراد نوح عليه السلام
